apps.localizedDescription: Standalone multi-provider AI usage monitor for Claude, ChatGPT, Antigravity, Grok, Google AI Studio, and OpenCode Go with secure local credential storage and device pairing.
apps.versionDescription:
Grok accounts can now use a saved limit reset from the account card, with the same confirmation as Claude and ChatGPT, instead of only listing it and sending you to grok.com.
On a wide window, the time since an account card's last update is now on its Refresh button ("⟳ 8m ago"), and the rename pencil only appears while you point at the card. Clicking the account's name, not just the pencil, starts renaming it.
The All Accounts subtitle now reads "Monitor 5-hour & 7-day limits and reset times across all your AI subscriptions."
Each usage bar on an account card now shows its reset on one line, such as "Resets in **4h 24m** · Today, 2:29p" or "Resets in **1d 6h** · Wed, Nov 18, 4:00a". Only the countdown is bold; resets later today say Today, and later days include the weekday.
On a wide window, the Settings page is now one centered column: the title, the line under it, and the cards share the same width, and the scrollbar sits right beside the cards instead of at the window's edge.
A saved limit reset now shows on its account card as one compact row with what it clears, when it expires, and a Use button, instead of a purple banner you had to open first. With more than one reset, the one that expires soonest is shown and the rest are one tap away.
Before you use a limit reset, the confirmation now names the account and how many resets it has left, and warns in an amber box what you'd actually get back from your current usage, for example that your 5-hour limit is already full so only 22% of your 7-day limit would come back. It also points out a limit that resets on its own within a day and a reset that expires within three days, and it updates if the account refreshes while it is open. The always-visible "cannot be undone" warning on the card is gone; the confirmation still says it.
Limit resets now say "7-day" instead of "weekly" ("Clears the 5-hour and 7-day limits"), matching the rest of the app.
On desktop, clicking an account's icon now shrinks just that card to the Compact view row, with all its usage bars and the next reset, instead of hiding everything but the lowest percentage. Clicking it again restores the full card. While Compact view is on, clicking an icon opens that one card in full, and pressing the Compact button puts every card back in the layout it picks.
The offline (QR code) transfer no longer asks you to compare a code on both screens. The sending device shows the animated codes with a Done button, and once the receiving device has scanned every frame it asks "Add 3 accounts from the other device?" with one Add Accounts button.
Linking two devices over Wi-Fi no longer asks you to compare a 12-character code on both screens. After the link code is entered, only the sending device asks you to press Send, and the receiving device waits for it.
The Dashboard summary strip now shows a single compact status line on both desktop and mobile ("All accounts good" when healthy, or an interactive amber "Attention needed" bar with a count that filters to cards needing attention and folds "Show all" into the same box), paired with the next reset countdown on the right.
On phones, when a custom group's name is too wide to share the title row with the Group badge, the Group badge now drops directly beneath the group name (centered together with the filter button) instead of hiding, and returns inline whenever there is enough room.
On phones, the box for renaming an account now sits on the line above the plan and status badges, so it stays wide enough to read the name instead of shrinking beside them.
Hovering over an account card's Refresh, Alerts, and rename buttons, a group's edit button, or Remove account in the card menu now fills the button in its own color with a white icon, matching the save and cancel buttons in the rename box.
The account list in the Create Group and Edit Group dialog now shows three accounts at a time instead of four; a fourth account brings in the scrollbar.
On phones, the red close button at the top of the accounts and groups drawer is slightly smaller, so it no longer looks larger than the filter button it replaces.
In Compact view on a wide window, each account row now has its Alerts button again, between Refresh and the menu.
Pressing Escape, or the Back button on Android, now cancels renaming an account even after the name box has lost focus.
An account card's actions menu is no longer cut off at the bottom edge of its card.
On phones, an account card's actions menu now stops above the bottom navigation bar and opens upward when there is not enough room below, instead of running off the screen.
In the Create Group and Edit Group dialog, the space above an error message now matches the space below it.
Linking devices over Wi-Fi now uses the six-digit link code as the secret that connects them. The code is never sent over the network, a device that doesn't know it can't reach your screen, and three wrong codes end the session so you need a new code. Both devices need this version to link.
A device receiving accounts now takes the other device's settings and layout only when "Also Transfer Settings & Layout" is ticked on the receiving device too. Before, only the sending device's choice counted.
On Android, the app no longer opens pairing links from other apps or websites. Linking starts only from Link Devices inside the app.
While the animated transfer codes of an offline (air-gapped) transfer are showing, the app window is now kept out of screenshots and screen recordings on Windows, macOS, and Android. On Android the app also shows blank in the recent-apps list during that time. iPhone and iPad cannot block screenshots, so the on-screen warning still applies there.
